question.leadin: This province's sovereignty movement grew stronger during its "Quiet Revolution."
question.text: Name this largest Canadian province, the only majority French-speaking one.
question.clue: Another leader of this region, Jacques Parizeau, blamed "money and the ethnic vote" for the outcome of a referendum.

swap.text: The Iroquois fought against Huron and Algonquin natives, as well as French trappers, in a series of wars thatare named for this dam-building animal, a primary target of French fur traders in the area.

question.text: This man was the first Prime Minister of Canada. He served in two separate terms after resigning due to the Pacific Railway Scandal, which saw Tory politicians bribed to give out prime rail routes.
question.clue: His government suppressed the Red River Rebellion by the Metis Louis Riel.

swap.leadin: A 1950s government led by this party saw Minister of Housing Harold Macmillan lead a construction boom and Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden support a coup d'etat in Iran.
swap.text: Name this British political party, which defeated the Labour Party of Clement Attlee in 1951 elections.
swap.clue: A foreign secretary from this party issued a statement supporting a "national home" in an Ottoman area.

question.leadin: This man's namesake "mania" followed his ascension to the head of the Liberal Party.
question.text: Name this man whose government enacted a Charter of Rights and Freedoms. He proclaimed "just watch me" three days before suspending the writ of habeas corpus under the War Measures Act.
question.clue: Peter Lougheed ("LAW-heed") opposed this leader's National Energy Program, which fixed prices after his country weathered two oil crises.

swap.leadin: Name the following, about the colonization of North America.
swap.text: This French explorer named Canada after the Iroquois word for "settlement."
swap.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

question.leadin: Answer the following about mass hysterias in history, none of which involve Pumpkin Spice Lattes.
question.text: In 1938, unsubstantiated reports of a "slasher" paralyzed a British town of this name. Another city of this name was leveled in 1917 by a massive ship explosion and provides Boston a Christmas tree every year as thanks for its subsequent aid.
question.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

swap.text: After de Gaulle's proclamation, this Canadian prime minister said that "Canadians do not need liberating." This leader formed the Royal Commission on the Status of Women while serving as Prime Minister from 1963 to 1968.
swap.clue: This politician claimed "Canadians do not need to be liberated" in response to the "Vive le Quebec Libre" speech another man gave at Expo 67.

question.text: He organized resistance to the Manitoba Act, which transferred Metis-populated lands from the Hudson's Bay Company to the Canadian government. For 15 points, name this leader of the Northwest Rebellion, who was hanged in 1885 for such opposition activity.
question.clue: This man's military general Gabriel Dumont was victorious at the Battle of Duck Lake, and he was forced into capture following defeat at the Battle of Batoche.

swap.text: This liberal opposition party in Canada elected Jagmeet Singh, the first Sikh leader of a major Canadian political party.
swap.clue: A major victory for this party was the surprise 1990 election of Bob Rae, but after a recession sapped their popularity, they dropped into third place in the 1995 elections in Ontario.

question.text: In 1970, Pierre Trudeau declared martial law in Quebec response to the October Crisis, in which British Trade Commissioner James Cross was kidnapped and provincial Labour Minister Pierre Laporte was murdered by this terrorist group.
question.clue: Members of this group kidnapped British Trade Commissioner James Cross and Minister of Labour and Immigration Pierre Laporte.

swap.leadin: Cuthbert Grant and his men won the Battle of Seven Oaks in this modern-day province.
swap.text: Name this province where Grant and his men killed Robert Semple and defeated the Hudson's Bay Company. A later rebellion in this province ended with the arrival of the Wolseley Expedition.
swap.clue: Due to an inability to acquire nails, rawhide cords called shaganappi were used in a colony in this province to fashion its namesake carts, used for transporting fur and bison products.

question.text: This financier was alleged to have paid off McDonald to win the Canadian Pacific contract.

swap.text: The Thule people, who spread east from Alaska and replaced the Dorset, were the ancestors of this ethnic group which now forms the majority of the populations of Nunavut and Greenland.
swap.answerHtml: Inuit [accept Inuk; prompt on (but correct) Eskimo; antiprompt on Kalaallit; antiprompt on Inuktitut; antiprompt on Iñupiaq; do NOT accept or prompt on “Innu” or “Yupik”] (The Innu are a Cree-speaking Algonquian people whose traditional lands confusingly border the southernmost extent of Inuit in Labrador.)
swap.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

question.leadin: The Sadlermiut were widely hypothesized to be the last remnants of this culture, until genetic studies revealed otherwise.
question.text: Name this culture that preceded the Thule. These people, named after a cape in Nunavut, inhabited much of the Canadian Arctic and Greenland.
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.leadin: Jean Chretien ("crate-YENN") led this party to a strong majority in the 1993 Canadian federal election.
swap.text: Name this centrist Canadian political party led from 1968 to 1984 by Pierre Trudeau.
swap.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Canada [or Parti libéral du Canada]
swap.clue: A request to dissolve parliament by a leader of this party was refused by Governor-General Julian Byng in 1926.

question.text: St. Laurent was defeated by this Conservative, who controversially ended Canada's domestic fighter jet industry.
question.clue: He also cancelled the Avro Arrow program, halting production of fighter jets in his country, when he signed NORAD with the US. Raised in Saskatchewan, he passed his country's Bill of Rights, and presided over the opening of the St. Lawrence Seaway.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a man who unfortunately is not Charles Tupper, but did replace Charles Tupper as the prime minister of Canada.
swap.text: This husband of the very homely Zoe Lafontaine created the Royal Canadian Navy with his Naval Service Bill.
swap.clue: This replacement of Charles Tupper created his nation's "tin pot" navy when he signed the Naval Service Bill.

question.leadin: This event is commemorated every December 6th with the ringing of a bell at a tower in Fort Needham Park.
question.text: Identify this event partially involving the SS Imo, which was flying a Norwegian flag. Some people were harmed by the 60-foot high tsunami during this event.
question.clue: One group killed in this event were sent by the Commission for Relief in Belgium, and this event destroyed the Horatio-Brannan- captained Stella Maris.

swap.text: The Popham settlement was a direct reaction to the St. Croix settlement of 1604, briefly capital of this French New World territory that notionally spanned the Bay of Fundy, Nova Scotia, and the Atlantic Coast of Canada.
swap.clue: This colony had its southern border with colonial Maine established along the Kennebec River.
